brand.name: McLaren
brand.tagline: British supercar maker, in India since 2022
brand.description: British supercar maker based in Woking; McLaren Automotive traces back to McLaren Cars, founded in 1985. McLaren entered India in 2022 through its official retailer Infinity Cars, whose McLaren Mumbai showroom in Prabhadevi is the brand's only Indian outlet; all cars are imported fully built.

models.name: 750S
highlights: 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with 750 PS and 800 Nm
Claimed 0–100 km/h in 2.8 s and 0–200 km/h in 7.2 s (Coupe)
Sold as a Coupe and as a Spider with a retractable hard top
McLaren says 750S production ends in 2027 (final orders accepted from Oct 2026)

variants.name: Spider
features: Retractable hard top, opens or closes in 11 s

models.notes: Price not published by the brand; from Autocar India. These are McLaren's revised India prices after the India–UK FTA (in force 15 Jul 2026): reported in June 2026 and restated by Autocar India on 9 Oct 2026 as Coupe Rs 4.94 crore and Spider Rs 5.46 crore before options. They are pan-India figures. Autocar India's model and Delhi price pages still show the older Rs 7.94 / 8.78 crore; check with McLaren Mumbai. Production ends in 2027. Top speed 332 km/h is McLaren's figure; Autocar India's launch report says 331. Boot is the 150-litre front compartment. Width includes mirrors. Airbags not officially published.

models.name: Artura
models.engine: 2993 cc twin-turbo V6 petrol + electric motor (plug-in hybrid)
models.power: 680 hp combined (700 PS on MY2025-on cars)

items: 7.4 kWh battery, up to 31 km electric-only range (claimed)
McLaren Carbon Lightweight Architecture carbon-fibre tub

highlights: Plug-in hybrid: 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 plus an axial-flux electric motor
7.4 kWh battery with up to 31 km of electric-only range (claimed)
Claimed 0–100 km/h in 3.0 s and a 330 km/h top speed
Built on McLaren's carbon-fibre Carbon Lightweight Architecture
Launched in India in May 2023 at Rs 5.1 crore (ex-showroom)
models.notes: Price not published by the brand; from Autocar India (Rs 5.10 crore ex-showroom Delhi, Nov 2026; Rs 5.1 crore ex-showroom Delhi at the 2023 launch). As a plug-in hybrid it gets no India–UK FTA duty cut, and reports say its price is unchanged. The Artura Spider has no Indian launch or price, so it is left out. Power is the India-launch figure (585 hp V6 + 95 hp motor). McLaren raised the combined output to 700 PS for MY2025, but the spec of current Indian cars is not confirmed. Autocar India's 21.74 kmpl is not an ARAI figure, so efficiency is null. McLaren plans to drop the Artura and GTS by 2028. Width includes mirrors. Airbags not officially published.

models.name: GTS

items: Nose-lift system: 130 mm clearance in about 4 s
Electronic parking brake with auto hold

highlights: 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with 635 PS and 630 Nm
570 litres of luggage space (420 L rear, 150 L front)
Claimed 0–100 km/h in 3.2 s and 0–200 km/h in 8.9 s
Replaced the McLaren GT; renamed GTS with the December 2023 facelift
models.notes: Price not published by the brand; from Autocar India, CarWale and AutoX (June 2026). They reported McLaren's revised India price after the India–UK FTA as Rs 3.83 crore, down from Rs 6.15 crore. Autocar India's GTS listing and Delhi price page still show Rs 6.15 crore (Nov 2026), and no later report confirms the GTS figure; check with McLaren Mumbai. Performance and luggage figures are McLaren's published figures, as reported at the Dec 2023 reveal. India launch date not published. McLaren plans to drop the GTS by 2028. Width includes mirrors. Airbags not officially published.
